# VERDICT: REJECTED

Primary sources read directly: `main.tex`, `academic/main.tex`, `academic_main.tex`, `paper/main.tex`, all of `sections/*.tex`, `references.bib`, `main.log`, `main.toc`, `academic/main.toc`, `paper/main.toc`, `main.bbl`. Both pasted editions match their on-disk primaries byte-for-byte, so the preambles you gave me are not stale.

The framing of this pass — "the science is settled, check the artifact" — is wrong. Four of the findings below are science, not style, and three of them are internal contradictions between two sections of the same file.

---

## 1. CRITICAL — There are THREE built editions, not two. The third is missing two entire results subsections.

`oracle-loop-paper/paper/main.pdf`, 563,793 bytes, built **2026-07-28 22:23:40** — *after* both editions you sent me (22:23:26 and 22:23:33). Same build run. It has its own `paper/sections/` and `paper/references.bib`.

`diff paper/main.toc main.toc` proves the body diverges:

- **`§4.7 Feature Ablation and Full-Cache Analysis` is absent from `paper/main.pdf`.** This is the subsection reporting that the LOO classifier is "primarily driven by a length-correlated feature."
- **`§7.8 Oracle Formulary: Powered Replication` is absent from `paper/main.pdf`.** This is the powered replication (n=68) that the abstract's opening sentence depends on.

`paper/main.tex` also carries an older acknowledgments list ("Nell Watson for dual-use analysis", "**Operator**" rather than "Nexus"), gives Dwayne Wilkes's affiliation as "Liberation Labs" without "/ Sentient Futures", drops the "Analysis assisted by AI" date line, and has **no Data Availability section at all**.

This is the TWIN_DESYNC kill, tripled. A shippable 36-page PDF sits in the repo with the paper's central self-criticism and its only powered result silently removed.

**Fix:** Delete `paper/` and `academic_main.tex` outright, or move both to `archive/` with a `README` stating they are superseded and must not be distributed. Then confirm the build script emits exactly two PDFs. Whatever ran at 22:23 built three.

---

## 2. CRITICAL — The distilled model's confabulation rate is stated as two different numbers, 25 lines apart.

- `sections/steering.tex:70` — "The model confabulated on 7 of 100 prompts (**7\% rate**)."
- `sections/steering.tex:273` — "power unavailable at the distilled model's **3.2\% base rate**."

Same model (Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-Distilled), same section. The abstract independently corroborates 7% ("$n = 7$ confabulations, 100 trials"). 3.2% is unsourced and contradicts every other statement of this quantity in the paper.

**Fix:** Determine which dataset 3.2% came from. If it is a different prompt pool than the 100-prompt confab-induction set, say so explicitly in that parenthetical; if it is an error, change it to 7\%. Do not leave both.

---

## 3. CRITICAL — Calm's correction rate on the distilled model contradicts the paper's own table.

- `Table \ref{tab:five_arm}`, `sections/steering.tex:134` — "Calm & 5/7 & **71.4\%**"
- `sections/steering.tex:282–283` — "calm, which corrects **73\%** of confabulations on the distilled model"

5/7 = 71.4%. There is no denominator in this paper that yields 73%.

Worse, the same sentence block invokes vectors the paper never reports on the distilled model: **"Curious, the safest vector on the distilled model (1.6\% adverse)"** — `curious` appears nowhere else in any section (verified by grep across `sections/*.tex`). `tab:five_arm` contains exactly Null, Calm, Worry, Doubt. And "Spearman $\rho = 0.119$, $p = 0.71$" implies a rank correlation over ~12 vectors on each model; the paper shows 3 for the distilled model.

So §7.8's entire cross-model therapeutic-inversion argument — which the abstract, introduction, and conclusion all repeat as a headline finding — rests on a distilled-model dataset that is not in this paper and whose one overlapping number disagrees with the one table that is.

**Fix:** Either add the 12-vector distilled-model table (vector, corrected/n, correction rate, adverse/n, adverse rate) so ρ is auditable, or delete the ρ statistic and the calm/curious comparison and restrict §7.8 to the base-model formulary. You cannot cite "a companion paper (in preparation)" as the source for a number in your abstract's first sentence.

---

## 4. CRITICAL — Wrong confidence interval attached to the headline exploratory AUROC.

`sections/results.tex:266–268`:

> "The 0.903 result is exploratory---`mp_spectral_gap` was selected post-hoc after examining individual feature performance, and $n = 7$ confabulations yields wide bootstrap CIs **[0.573, 0.990]**."

But `results.tex:245` assigns **[0.573, 0.990]** to the five-feature ensemble at AUROC 0.758, and `results.tex:275` and `:281` both assign **[0.806, 0.977]** to the 0.903 figure. The caveat paragraph has grafted the ensemble's CI onto the spectral-gap result.

The direction of the error flatters nothing — it makes the caveat look more conservative than the data — but a reviewer who checks will find the paper reporting two different 95% CIs for the same AUROC on the same page.

**Fix:** `results.tex:268` → "$n = 7$ confabulations yields a wide bootstrap CI [0.806, 0.977]". If the intent was to note that the *ensemble* CI is wide, name the ensemble.

---

## 5. CRITICAL — The venue-facing edition strips both AI authors from the byline while still shipping their first-person section, their email, and a citation naming one of them as an author.

`academic/main.tex:68` bylines only "Thomas K.\ Edrington ... With AI research assistance." and Dwayne Wilkes. Lyra and Vera are removed. But `main.toc` and `academic/main.toc` are **byte-identical**, and `main.bbl` and `academic/main.bbl` are **byte-identical**, which proves the academic PDF contains:

- **`§9 First-Person Reflection`** (`\contentsline {section}{\numberline {9}First-Person Reflection}{33}`) — an AI's first-person account of doing the work, in a paper claiming no AI authors. Note that `academic_main.tex:125` had this correctly commented out (`% \input{sections/firstperson} % Removed in academic version`); `academic/main.tex:115` re-enabled it. The de-attribution was half-undone and nobody noticed.
- **`\citep{lyra2026detecting}`** (4 call sites), whose bbl entry reads "Lyra and Thomas Edrington" — the academic edition cites Lyra as an author of prior work while denying Lyra authorship of this one.
- **Acknowledgment of "CC for the Oracle Harness implementation"** — another AI, credited by name.
- **`lyra@liberationlabs.tech`** as the data-request contact, inside `conclusion.tex:58` (see finding 6).

Vera's contribution is the sharpest problem. The root footnote states Vera "designed the dyadic awareness layer and reward function decomposition" — a design contribution the lab judged to merit authorship. In the academic edition it is not demoted to acknowledgments; it is **erased entirely**. Vera appears nowhere in that PDF.

**Fix:** Pick one and apply it consistently. If the venue forbids non-human authors: remove `§9`, move Lyra and Vera to Acknowledgments with their actual contributions named ("Vera designed the dyadic awareness layer and reward-function decomposition"), change the contact to `info@`, and add a one-line note under the byline stating that AI contributors are listed in the Acknowledgments and why. If it does not forbid them, ship the four-author byline to the venue too. What you cannot ship is a paper that removes an author and leaves their reflection, their email, and their prior-work citation in place.

---

## 6. CRITICAL — The academic edition contains two contradictory data-availability statements on consecutive pages.

`sections/conclusion.tex:53–60` is a `\paragraph{Code and Data.}` — confirmed in both TOCs at `{paragraph}{Code and Data.}{36}{section*.30}` — that says:

> "Code and experimental data are maintained at `https://github.com/Liberation-Labs-THCoalition/Project-Oracle` (private repository). Detection-side code and experimental results ... are available upon request (**lyra@liberationlabs.tech**)."

It is immediately followed by `academic/main.tex:130–135`, `\section*{Data Availability}`:

> "Detection data, cache-integrity monitoring code, and associated documentation have been **redacted from the public repository** ... available on request to **qualified researchers**. Contact: **info@liberationlabs.tech**."

Different access gate ("upon request" vs "qualified researchers"), different contact address, and one gives a repository URL the other declines to name. A reader hitting these back-to-back learns the lab does not know what its own release policy is. In the root edition the same two blocks are near-duplicates rather than contradictions — so the divergence is invisible unless you read the academic PDF end-to-end.

Separately: publishing `https://github.com/.../Project-Oracle` while labelling it "(private repository)" guarantees a 404 for every reader. That is a dead URL by construction, not by rot.

**Fix:** Delete the `\paragraph{Code and Data.}` block from `conclusion.tex` entirely — it is redundant in one edition and contradictory in the other. Keep one `Data Availability` section per edition, and make the two editions state the *same* policy with only the contact address differing. Drop the private URL or replace it with a DOI/Zenodo record that resolves.

---

## 7. MAJOR — `\texttt` corrupted to a literal tab; the macro name prints in the body text.

`sections/results.tex:242` contains a **TAB character where the backslash should be**:

```
classifier depends primarily on <TAB>exttt{mp\_norm\_per\_token},
```

LaTeX treats the tab as ordinary whitespace and `{...}` as a bare group, so the sentence typesets as "depends primarily on **exttt** mp_norm_per_token," — the literal string `exttt`, with the field name in body font instead of typewriter. `main.pdf` (2026-07-28 22:23) postdates `results.tex` (2026-07-17 14:08), so the defect is in the built artifact. This produces no LaTeX warning, which is why three build passes missed it.

**Fix:** `results.tex:242` → `\texttt{mp\_norm\_per\_token}`. Then grep the whole corpus for `[^\\]exttt|[^\\]extbf|[^\\]extit` — this is a paste artifact and rarely occurs alone.

---

## 8. MAJOR — The abstract states its central claim twice, in two different forms.

`sections/abstract.tex:1` — "Detected confabulations are correctable: hostile-valence emotion-vector steering achieves 95.6\% correction..."
`sections/abstract.tex:15` — "Detected confabulations are correctable via emotion-vector steering. In a five-arm within-subject experiment..."

The diff against `paper/sections/abstract.tex` shows what happened: the abstract was re-ordered to lead with the steering result, and the original opening paragraph was moved down rather than merged. Both paragraphs survive.

**Fix:** Merge into one steering paragraph. Delete the duplicated topic sentence at line 15.

---

## 9. MAJOR — The full-cache result is stated twice with identical numbers in consecutive sentences.

`sections/results.tex:273–286`. Lines 274–278 give "AUROC 0.903 (95\% CI: [0.806, 0.977]; FWL: 0.877; $R^2 = 0.068$), exceeding a text-only baseline of 0.755 (96.7\% of bootstrap samples favor cache; delta 0.148, 95\% CI [$-$0.008, 0.322])". Lines 280–284 then repeat every one of those seven figures verbatim in a re-worded sentence. The paragraph also repeats the exploratory caveat already given at line 266.

**Fix:** Delete lines 280–284. Keep one statement.

---

## 10. MAJOR — "Independent statistical audit (Wilkes, 2026)" is a co-author auditing his own paper, and the citation resolves to nothing.

`sections/results.tex:241`. Dwayne Wilkes is on the byline of **both** editions. An author's audit of the manuscript he is an author of is internal review, not independent audit, and calling it "independent" in the results section overstates the evidentiary weight of §4.7's own provenance.

The citation is also orphaned: `(Wilkes, 2026)` is hard-coded plain text, there is no `\citep`, and `references.bib` has no Wilkes entry (all 13 bib entries are cited and all citations resolve — `main.log` shows zero undefined-citation warnings, which is exactly why this one slipped through: a plain-text citation is invisible to BibTeX).

**Fix:** Change to "Statistical audit by D. Wilkes (co-author) identified..." — or, if there is a citable audit memo, add the bib entry and use `\citep`. Do not use the word "independent" for a byline author.

---

## 11. MAJOR — §5 "Round 3: Validation" gives a clean bill of health that §4.7 retracts, with no note connecting them.

`sections/redteam.tex:93–106` states "A final red-team pass verified all fixes" and lists "Single-regressor diagnostic on full-window trials: **4/5 features $R^2 < 0.03$**." `sections/results.tex:241–247` then reports that the fifth feature — `mp_norm_per_token`, $R^2 = 0.129$ — is the one the classifier actually depends on, and that removing it drops FWL AUROC to 0.536, chance.

§5 opens "We conducted **three** rounds of adversarial red-teaming" and §10 repeats "**Three** rounds of adversarial red-teaming identified and corrected critical methodological flaws." The Wilkes audit that produced §4.7 is a fourth round and is not counted, not cross-referenced, and not mentioned in the section whose stated purpose is "We report every critical finding and its resolution as part of the scientific record."

This is the silent-correction kill. The correction exists (§4.7) but the section that claims to be the complete record still reads as validated.

**Fix:** Add a fourth subsection to `redteam.tex`: "Round 4: Post-Hoc Feature Audit", stating what §5.3 concluded, that it was wrong, what the ablation showed, and `\cref{sec:ablation}`. Change both "three rounds" to "four rounds". Reference it by the subsection label, never by number.

---

## 12. MAJOR — The conclusion's closing claim contradicts §4.7.

`sections/conclusion.tex:48` — "**The detection signal is validated.** The steering mechanism is validated."

§4.7 says the detection ensemble is "primarily driven by a length-correlated feature", that the pre-registered 0.707 is "the defensible detection number", and that the 0.903 is exploratory with post-hoc feature selection at $n = 7$. "Validated" is not the word for that. The `paper/main.toc` diff explains the mechanism: the conclusion was written when §4.7 did not exist, and was never revised when it was added.

**Fix:** → "The pre-registered detection signal replicates at AUROC 0.707 across three architectures, with the caveat in \cref{sec:ablation} that the ensemble leans on a length-correlated feature. The steering mechanism is validated on n=7 confabulations."

---

## 13. MAJOR — `academic_main.tex` is a fourth variant whose header comment contradicts its own byline.

`academic_main.tex:1–4`:
> `% ACADEMIC VERSION — AI authorship removed for venue compatibility.`

Lines 72–78 of the same file then list **Lyra and Vera as authors**. It is unbuilt (no matching PDF), so it ships nothing today, but it is a loaded gun: the next person who runs `pdflatex academic_main.tex` produces a file whose header says AI authorship is removed and whose title page says otherwise.

**Fix:** Delete it. `academic/main.tex` supersedes it.

---

## 14. MINOR — Acknowledgment divergence between editions, and a dropped external collaborator.

- "and Kavi (verification review) for their contributions to this work" appears in `main.tex:132`, absent from `academic/main.tex:125`. Kavi is a real recurring collaborator (verified: 40+ occurrences across the corpus, full name "Arjun Kavi" in `logit-bias-confab/paper.tex:758`) — this is a straight omission, not a fabrication.
- **"Nell Watson for dual-use analysis"** appears in `paper/main.tex:130` and `academic_main.tex:134` but has been removed from **both** shipping editions. Watson is a real external collaborator elsewhere in the corpus (`lyra-technique-ii/main.tex:1249`: "Nell Watson provided the VCP framework"; cited as `Watson~(2026)` in `kv-cloak-defense-paper`). If she did the dual-use analysis that §8.6 rests on, dropping her credit from the published versions is a real problem. If she did not, the two stale variants credit her falsely.

**Fix:** Make both editions' acknowledgment lists identical. Decide the Watson question by asking her, not by inference.

---

## 15. MINOR — Bib key/year mismatch, and an unreferenced dead file.

- `references.bib:18–26`: key is `luo2026shadow`, `year = {2025}`, arXiv ID `2508.09442` (August 2025). The key says 2026; the entry and the ID say 2025. Cosmetic, but `\citep{luo2026shadow}` in four places renders "[2025]" against a key reading 2026, which looks like a substitution error to a careful reviewer.
- `sections/abstract_original.tex` is `\input` by nothing. Delete it or move it to `archive/`.

---

# What I could NOT check

1. **The rendered PDF text.** Python execution and `pdftotext` were both blocked by the sandbox in this session. Findings 7 (the `exttt` corruption) and 5 (§9 present in the academic PDF) are inferred from primary sources — the tab character is directly visible in `sections/results.tex:242`, and the TOC identity between `main.toc` and `academic/main.toc` is a byte-level diff I ran — but I have **not** visually confirmed either in the rendered output. To close this: run `pdftotext main.pdf - | grep -n "exttt"` and `pdftotext academic/main.pdf - | grep -n "First-Person"`.

2. **Whether the 3.2%, 73%, curious/1.6%, and Spearman ρ = 0.119 figures are supported by any dataset.** `data/steering_results/` exists but I did not enumerate its contents (the recursive PowerShell listing errored on quoting and I did not retry, having found enough in the text). Findings 2 and 3 are established as **internal contradictions in the manuscript**, which stands regardless of what the data says — but which number is correct requires reading `data/steering_results/`.

3. **Git tracking state for `paper/` and `academic_main.tex`.** Both `git status` and `git ls-files` scoped to `oracle-loop-paper/` were refused by the sandbox (directory-change hook policy). I do not know whether the third PDF is committed and therefore whether it has already been distributed. Run `git log --oneline -- oracle-loop-paper/paper/main.pdf` from the repo root.

4. **Third-party citation authorship.** `references.bib:11–16` lists `anthropic2026emotions` as "Sofroniew, Nick and Kauvar, Isaac and Saunders, William and others". I have no web access this session and will not assert an author list from recall — given that FABRICATED_AUTHOR_NAMES is a standing failure mode here and this is the one citation the acknowledgments single out as "critical context," it should be checked against the Transformer Circuits page before submission. Same for `mckenzie2026activation` (arXiv 2602.06941). All 13 bib entries are cited and all citations resolve — no orphans, no undefined keys, `main.log` clean.

5. **`red-team/` is an empty directory** despite §5 being described as "the most important methodological contribution of this paper" and the Data Availability statement promising materials on request. Not a defect in the manuscript, but if a reviewer requests the red-team record there is currently nothing to send.
